draft.subject: Computer Vision Engineer application, false positives and edge deployment
draft.body:
My name is Justin Mascarenhas and I have an M.S. in Computer Engineering from Rochester Institute of Technology. I applied for the Computer Vision Engineer opening and wanted to reach out since you run detection as a product.

Most of my computer vision work has ended on a device rather than in a notebook. For my graduate capstone I put a YOLO detector through TensorRT on a Jetson for a robot picking objects in real time. The model was the easy part. Cutting false positive detections and handling stale camera frames took far longer, since a confident wrong detection did more damage than a missed one.

The same trade off likely shows up at Pano AI, where a false alarm costs a fire agency trust. Detection that holds up outdoors on live feeds is the problem I want to work on.

I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss the role further, if your time allows. I can share my resume if that would be helpful.
draft.hook_used: False positive tradeoff: as Detection PM his core metric is alert fatigue; capstone centered on debugging false positives
